mechanism_claims.claim_text: Active lugdunin analogues correlate antimicrobial activity with dissipation of S. aureus NCTC8325 membrane potential.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: lugdunin and selected active/inactive analogues tested in this paper

source_locator.locator: xml:fig=3 and body paragraphs around Figure 3

mechanism_claims.limitations: Supports membrane-potential dissipation, not a specific protein target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Lugdunin does not form large pores or gross membrane lesions under the tested conditions.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: lugdunin compound 1 compared with pore-forming or membrane-disrupting controls
mechanism_claims.limitations: Excludes large-pore/lesion behavior in the assayed contexts; does not exclude all possible membrane interactions.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Lugdunin promotes proton translocation across artificial POPC vesicles while maintaining membrane integrity.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: lugdunin compound 1 in pyranine/HPTS vesicle assays

supplementary_sources: paper_packets/doi__10.1002_anie.201901589/extracted/supplementary_text/ANIE-58-9234-s001.txt:vesicle preparation and proton transport assay context

mechanism_claims.limitations: Directly supports proton transport in synthetic vesicles; carrier versus channel formation remains unresolved by the paper.

quality_controls.detail: Every mechanism claim has a stable claim_id.
Direct mechanism claims list direct assay types.
Every claim has XML and/or supplement locators.
Claims do not promote a specific protein target or unresolved carrier/channel distinction.

caution_findings.note: Mechanism is accepted for membrane potential/proton translocation evidence; the paper leaves carrier versus channel formation unresolved.
